'''Benedek Jávor''' (born 2 July 1972) is a Hungarian politician and a former [[Member of the European Parliament]] (MEP) from 2014 to 2019. He is a member of [[Dialogue for Hungary]], part of the [[European Green Party]].

==Biography==
He finished his secondary studies at the [[Benedictine High School of Pannonhalma]]. He graduated in biology at the [[ELTE Faculty of Science|Faculty of Science]] of the [[Eötvös Loránd University]] in 1997 (MSc), and in 2006 he received his [[Ph.D.]] at the same university. He has been assistant professor at the department of [[environmental law]] at the [[Pázmány Péter Catholic University]].

In 2000 he was a founding member of the environmental NGO ''[[Védegylet NGO|Védegylet]]'' (Protect the Future!). He was an active organizer to support the election of [[László Sólyom]] as [[President of Hungary]]. In 2009 he was a founding member and one of the spokespersons of the [[Politics Can Be Different]] party. In the [[2010 Hungarian parliamentary election|parliamentary election in 2010]] he won a seat in the [[National Assembly of Hungary|National Assembly]]. He served as Chairman of the Committee on Sustainable Development between 2010 and 2013. He was the LMP party's candidate for the position of [[Mayor of Budapest]] in the [[2010 Budapest mayoral election]]. He received 9.89% of the vote and came to the third place. After the resignation of [[András Schiffer]] he was appointed leader of the LMP [[parliamentary group]] on 29 January 2012.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://index.hu/belfold/2012/01/29/frakciovezetot_valaszt_az_lmp/ |title=Jávor Benedek az LMP új frakcióvezetője
 |publisher=[[Index.hu]] |accessdate = 2012-01-29}}</ref> During the party's congress in November 2012, the Politics Can Be Different decided not to join [[Together 2014]], the electoral alliance of opposition parties and movements led by [[Gordon Bajnai]]. As a result Jávor, a follower of the agreement, resigned from his position of parliamentary group leader.<ref>{{cite web|accessdate=2012-11-18|url=http://hvg.hu/itthon/20121118_LMP_Bajnai_kongresszus_Javor_Schiffer|title=Beintett Bajnainak az LMP, lemondott Jávor Benedek|date=18 November 2012}}</ref>

In January 2013, the LMP's congress rejected against the electoral cooperation with other opposition forces, including Together 2014.<ref>{{cite web|accessdate=2013-02-08|url=http://www.politics.hu/20130127/lmp-rejects-proposals-for-new-strategy-at-party-congress/|title=LMP rejects proposals for new strategy at party congress|date=27 January 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130927150336/http://www.politics.hu/20130127/lmp-rejects-proposals-for-new-strategy-at-party-congress/|archive-date=27 September 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> As a result members of LMP’s “Dialogue for Hungary” platform, under the leadership of Jávor, announced their decision to leave the opposition party and form a new organization. Benedek Jávor said the eight MPs leaving LMP would keep their parliamentary mandates. The leaving MPs established Dialogue for Hungary as a full-fledged party.<ref>{{cite web|accessdate=2013-02-08|url=http://www.politics.hu/20130204/lmp-rebels-to-establish-dialogue-for-hungary-as-a-full-fledged-party/|title=LMP rebels to establish Dialogue for Hungary as a full-fledged party|date=4 February 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130927150414/http://www.politics.hu/20130204/lmp-rebels-to-establish-dialogue-for-hungary-as-a-full-fledged-party/|archive-date=27 September 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref>

The Dialogue for Hungary (PM) held its inaugural congress on 17 February 2013. Jávor was elected co-president of the party, alongside [[Tímea Szabó]]. The congress also authorized the party's presidency to open the negotiations with Together 2014.<ref>{{cite web|accessdate=2013-02-17|url=http://index.hu/belfold/2013/02/17/javor_benedek_es_szabo_timea_vezetik_a_parbeszed_magyarorszagert_tomorulest/|title=Jávor Benedek és Szabó Tímea vezetik a Párbeszéd Magyarországért tömörülést|date=17 February 2013}}</ref> On 8 March 2013, the PM entered into an alliance with the Together 2014, which officially formed as a political party. Jávor and Szabó, co-chairs of the PM also became members of the Together 2014's board.<ref>{{cite web|accessdate=2013-03-09|url=http://www.politics.hu/20130309/former-pm-bajnais-political-movement-officially-forms-political-party/|title=Former PM Bajnai's political movement officially forms political party|date=9 March 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140202092645/http://www.politics.hu/20130309/former-pm-bajnais-political-movement-officially-forms-political-party/|archive-date=2 February 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Jávor was elected [[Member of the European Parliament]] (MEP) in the [[2014 European Parliament election in Hungary|2014 European Parliament election]] and joined [[The Greens–European Free Alliance]] (Greens/EFA). In June 2014, he was replaced as co-chair of the party by [[Gergely Karácsony]].<ref>{{cite web|accessdate=2014-06-16|url=http://hvg.hu/itthon/20140615_Javor_helyett_Karacsonyt_valasztottak_a_P|title=Karácsony: Új társelnök az Együtt-PM-ben|date=2014-06-15}}</ref> His name appeared in the joint list of the [[Hungarian Socialist Party]] (MSZP) and the Dialogue for Hungary during the [[2019 European Parliament election in Hungary|2019 European Parliament election]], but did not win a mandate.<ref>{{cite web|accessdate=2019-07-02|url=https://index.hu/belfold/2019/05/26/javor_benedek_allast_keresek/|title=Jávor Benedek: Állást keresek|date=2019-05-26}}</ref> In 2019, Jávor was the recipient of the Environment Award at ''The Parliament Magazine'''s annual [[The Parliament Magazine#The MEP Awards|MEP Awards]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theparliamentmagazine.eu/articles/event-coverage/mep-awards-2019-heartfelt-reactions-our-winners|title=MEP Awards 2019: Heartfelt reactions from our winners|last=Hutchinson|first=Lorna|date=21 March 2019|work=[[The Parliament Magazine]]|accessdate=13 August 2019}}</ref>

He was appointed as head of the official representation of [[Budapest]] (led by mayor Gergely Karácsony, fellow Dialogue member) in [[Brussels]] on 1 January 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://budapest.hu/varoshaza/fovarosi-onkormanyzat/varosdiplomacia/budapest-fovaros-brusszeli-kepviselete |title=Budapest Főváros Brüsszeli Képviselete |accessdate=2025-04-03}}</ref> He was appointed board member of the [[Green European Foundation]] in October 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://gef.eu/about-gef/people-and-structure/board-of-directors/ |title=Board of Directors, GEF |accessdate=2025-04-03}}</ref>

==Personal life==
He is married and has two children.<ref>[https://parbeszedmagyarorszagert.hu/hu/kepviselo/javor-benedek Bendek Jávor Biography]</ref>
